summary: Johann Gustav Stickel worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Jena (1823–1826) and under Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He served as professor at Jena from 1830 to 1836.
Johann Jakob Engel was a philosopher who studied at the University of Rostock (~1757–1761) and the University of Leipzig (~1761–1765). He also taught Wilhelm von Humboldt.

Johann Tobias Beck was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tübingen (~1822–1826) and later held posts at the University of Basel (~1836–1843) and the University of Tübingen (~1843–1878).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff worked in Indology and other fields. Educated at Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen, he held posts at Tübinger Stift, the University of Tartu, Melanchthon-Gymnasium Nürnberg, the University of Würzburg, and FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg.

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at Leiden and Utrecht (under Jan Gonda). She taught Sanskrit at Groningen, lectured at Cambridge, and directed Amsterdam's Institute of South Asian Archaeology (1958–1983).

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She studied at Saarland University under Ernst Zinn and completed her PhD at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg under Karl Hoffmann, where she later served as an assistant (1973–1977).

Johannes Beltz specializes in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD studies at the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études by 1999, supervised by Marie-Louise Reiniche and Johannes Bronkhorst.

Johannes Bronkhorst works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Educated at VU Amsterdam, Rajasthan, Pune (under S. D. Joshi), and Leiden, he held posts at Instituut Kern, Leiden, and as professor at the University of Lausanne (1987–2011).

Johannes Hertel was an Indologist who earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Leipzig (1892–1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920) before holding the chair of Indian philology at the University of Leipzig from 1919 to 1937.

Johannes Klatt was an Indologist who studied under Albrecht Weber and earned his doctorate at the University of Halle (~1869–1873). From 1872 onward, he worked at the Prussian State Library, advancing from part-time staff to custodian and librarian.

Johannes Nobel worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Greifswald and Berlin (PhD under Heinrich Lüders). After posts at the Prussian State Library and Berlin, he held the Indology chair at Marburg (1928–1955).

Johannes Rahder worked in Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate at Utrecht (~1920–1926). He held professorships at Utrecht (1930–1931), Leiden (1931–1946), and Yale (1947–1965), and also held posts at the University of Hawaiʻi.

Johannes Schmidt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Bonn and at Jena under August Schleicher, as well as under Albrecht Weber. He held professorships at Bonn (1868), Graz (1873–1876), and Berlin (1876).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. After earning a Magister at Marburg (1986–1992), he held posts at FU Berlin, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and Munich, where he became an adjunct professor in 2014.

Johannes Schubert worked in Tibetology and Sinology, studying at Leipzig and under scholars including Conrady and Francke. He served at the Leipzig University Library (~1927–1954) and taught Tibetan and Mongolian at the University of Leipzig between 1934 and 1962.

John A. Ardussi works in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He studied for his MA under Turrell V. Wylie and earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 1977). He has held research roles at the CNRS and worked at ELDEC Corporation.

John Alexander Jorgensen works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He completed an MA at the Australian National University under Kenneth Herbert Joseph Gardiner in 1979 and held posts at the Australian National University and Griffith University.

John Alexander Stewart worked in linguistics and other fields. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1899–1903), served in the Indian Civil Service (~1905–1933), and held posts at University College London (~1933–1936) and SOAS (~1936–1948).

John Allan was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist educated at Edinburgh and Leipzig. He served at the British Museum (from 1907; Keeper of Coins and Medals, 1931) and lectured in Sanskrit at UCL, SOAS, and the University of Edinburgh.

John Avery was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Amherst College, the universities of Tübingen and Berlin, and under William Dwight Whitney (~1867–1870). He served as Professor of Greek at Grinnell College (1870–1877) and Bowdoin College (1877).
